notes: Verified 21-Aug-2026, then RE-verified live on 21-Aug-2026 (Phase 2 build) via a fresh browser-driven fetch of the raw response. The re-check corrected an assumption from the first pass: the homepage's scrolling ticker ('.rating-content.simply-scroll-list li', formerly documented as the primary selector) is actually populated by client-side JavaScript — it is NOT present in the raw HTTP response, only in the live DOM after the page's own scripts run. The '/Home/rate_board' card layout, however, genuinely is server-rendered and IS present in the raw response with no JS required. The primary/secondary roles below have been swapped from the first draft to reflect this. The site does not serve a working HTTPS version (https:// redirects back to http://) — use the http URL. SECOND CORRECTION (21-Aug-2026, after the first live GitHub Actions run returned EXTRACTION_ERROR): the site's card wrapper changed from a CSS class '.smallBox3' to an HTML id (id="smallBox3") on a element now carrying the class 'ratebox-table-wrap' instead — '.smallBox3' as a class selector now matches zero elements. Everything nested inside the card (the '.flag-country-rating-head' heading and '.flag-country-rating-list' buy/sell rows) is unchanged. cardBlockSelector below was updated from '.smallBox3' to '.ratebox-table-wrap' and re-verified live to match all 8 currency cards on the page, CNY included (Buy 60.35 / Sell 60.60 observed at verification time). This is exactly the 'SOURCE STRUCTURE MAY HAVE CHANGED' scenario the project brief anticipated (section 23) — the system correctly reported EXTRACTION_ERROR rather than showing stale or fabricated data as LIVE.
requiresBrowserAutomationReason: The '/Home/rate_board' card layout's BUY/SELL values were confirmed present in the raw server-rendered HTML via a fetch independent of any browser JS execution (re-verified 21-Aug-2026). A plain HTTP GET + HTML parser (cheerio) is sufficient for the primary path.
playwrightFallbackReason: If the site migrates this page to client-side rendering in the future, plain-fetch extraction will start failing validation (fails safe, never silently stale). The Playwright fallback re-uses the exact same selectors against the rendered DOM of the same URL, so it keeps working whether or not JS involvement changes.
branchNotes: No branch/location selector was found on the public site; My Money Master publishes a single site-wide rate per currency.

primarySelector.description: Per-country card on the Exchange Rate page. Each currency is a '.ratebox-table-wrap' block (formerly '.smallBox3' as a class — the site now uses that string as a literal, non-unique id instead; see 'notes' above) containing a '.flag-country-rating-head' (the currency's full display name, e.g. 'Chinese Renminbi' — NOT the ISO code) followed by two '.flag-country-rating-list' sibling divs, one for Buy and one for Sell, each holding two plain <span>s: a label ('Buy :' / 'Sell :') and the numeric value.
primarySelector.matchStrategy: For each '.ratebox-table-wrap' block, read '.flag-country-rating-head' text and match it against config.currencyDisplayNames[currencyCode] (exact, trimmed). Within the matching block, read each '.flag-country-rating-list' div's two child <span>s: first span's text (case-insensitive, colon-stripped) tells you Buy vs Sell; second span's text is the numeric value.

primarySelector.liveSampleObservedAt: 2026-08-21 (second re-verification, after fixing the merge-conflict-broken CI run): CNY BUY 60.35 / SELL 60.60

secondarySelector.description: DEMOTED as of the Phase 2 re-verification — this was originally documented as the primary selector, but is confirmed to require JavaScript execution (not present in the raw HTTP response). Kept here only as the target for the Playwright fallback path, or if a future adapter revision prefers it once JS-rendered.
secondarySelector.note: Confirmed via fetch(location.href) from within the live page context returning HTML that does NOT contain this element or text, while document.querySelector('.rating-content li') against the already-loaded DOM does. A raw HTTP GET (no JS) will not see this ticker's content.

waitStrategy.httpFetch: none required for the primary ('/Home/rate_board' card) selector — values are present on initial response
waitStrategy.playwrightFallback: navigate to liveRateUrl, wait for '.ratebox-table-wrap .flag-country-rating-head' to be attached, then read as with the HTTP path (same selectors, rendered DOM)

validation.notes: Range is a sanity bound only, not a hard limit — widen per-currency ranges as real historical data accumulates. Reject a reading where BUY > SELL, or where the value looks like it's missing the /100 unit scaling (e.g. 0.60 instead of 60).
